guide.nexium.power.power:
Nexus Energy
Every farm and the Freezer runs on Nexus Energy (NE). A machine uses a set amount each tick it works, and stops when it has none; its screen says how much it needs.

Plant and block farms: 10 NE/t. Mob farms and the Freezer: 20. The Iron Farm: 40.

A machine holds ten seconds of energy.

Overclock: the OC button on a farm's or the Freezer's screen makes it x2, x4 or x8: that many times faster for that many times the NE/t, the same energy per cycle. Short of energy it runs as fast as it can pay for.
guide.nexium.power.generator:
Combustion Generator
Burns wood, charcoal, coal or any other furnace fuel, for as long as it would burn in a furnace, and makes 40 NE/t: a piece of coal is 64,000 NE.

It gives its energy to the machines touching it, and lights the next piece only when it has room for more. Hoppers feed the fuel.
guide.nexium.power.solar:
Solar Panel
Makes 30 NE/t while the sun is up, 8 NE/t in rain, and nothing at night or under a roof: it needs open sky above it. It stores 5,000 NE.

It costs nothing to run, so a few of them beside a Battery carry a plant farm through the night.
guide.nexium.power.thermal:
Thermal Generator
Burns lava into 80 NE/t. A bucket lasts about eight minutes (800,000 NE). Fill it with a lava bucket, or let a Fluid Intake or a fluid conduit feed it: it takes lava only.

With an Infinite Lava Source beside a Fluid Intake it never runs dry.
guide.nexium.power.reactor:
Redstone Reactor
The top generator. Nine Redstone Fuel Rods make 200 NE/t each at the default depth: 1,800 NE/t with all nine, and it runs on any one to nine.

Insert or Retract moves every rod together, five steps from -2 (100 NE/t a rod) through 0, the default (200), to +2 (300). Deeper rods make more power but heat and wear much faster.

Heat is carried off by ice in the three coolant slots; blue ice cools best and lasts longest (ice 30 seconds a piece, packed ice a minute, blue ice two minutes). The tank holds 16 buckets of water (fill it by bucket, Fluid Intake or fluid conduit): water cools only above 59.9% heat, taking off just what it takes to hold the core there, and uses up to a bucket every 30 seconds. Three slots of blue ice and water together hold nine rods at +2 on 59.9% heat and the full 2,700 NE/t. Output holds to 60% heat, falls steadily from there, and at 90% the reactor shuts off until it is under 50% again. It never explodes.

A rod lasts 96 hours at the default depth, then leaves a Spent Fuel Rod: craft it with eight Redstone Blocks for a fresh rod.
guide.nexium.power.furnace:
Nexus Furnace
Eight input slots, each with an output slot of its own, all cooking at once on Nexus Energy. It smelts, blasts and smokes: anything a furnace, a blast furnace or a smoker cooks.

Each item takes 2.5 seconds, and each slot that is working uses 30 NE/t (240 NE/t for all eight). With less power than that it runs as many slots as it can pay for, taking turns.

A stack you put in, by hand, shift-click, hopper or pipe, is shared out evenly over the input slots. Hoppers and pipes go in from the top and sides and take out from below. It gives ten times the experience the recipes do, kept in the furnace: press the button on its screen to collect it.
guide.nexium.power.battery:
Batteries
Iron holds 250,000 NE, Gold 1,000,000 and Diamond 10,000,000. Generators and Energy Conduits fill them; conduits and the machines touching them take from them.

Six cells on the side show the charge, and a comparator reads it. Break one and it keeps its charge, and gives it back when placed again.
guide.nexium.power.cells:
Battery cells
Small batteries that hold charge in the item: the Iron Cell holds 250,000 NE, the Gold Cell 1,000,000 and the Diamond Cell 10,000,000, like the Batteries of the same name. The bar under the item shows how full it is.

They power the Jetpack and the Crafting Storage Tablet, which each have a slot for one, and they are charged in a Charging Station.
guide.nexium.power.station:
Charging Station
Four slots for battery cells, or for a Jetpack or Tablet with a cell in it: it charges them from what it takes in from touching Energy Conduits and Batteries (it holds 20,000 NE itself). It can charge 4,000 NE a tick in all, shared by the cells that are charging: one cell takes all 4,000, two take 2,000 each, and all four 1,000 each. A bar under each slot shows the charge.
guide.nexium.jetpack.jetpack:
Jetpack
Right-click to wear it in the wings slot (or the chest slot), so a chestplate can be worn too. It flies on a battery cell kept in its own screen: sneak and right-click it, or press J (Controls > Key Binds) while it is worn.

Jump in the air to take off. Then jump rises, letting go hovers, and sneaking sinks. It uses 8 NE a tick while jump is held and 4 hovering; when the cell is empty you fall.

Two keys, unbound until you set them in Controls > Key Binds, switch the engine off and on (off: no flight and no power use) and hover off and on. With hover off, hold jump to thrust and rise, and let go to drop. It takes the armor enchantments an elytra does, all four Protections at once, and Thorns and the curses. It does not glide.
guide.nexium.power.conduit:
Conduits and Energy
The Conduit carries Nexus Energy from generators to machines along with items and fluids: 2,500 NE/t (Tier 1) or 50,000 NE/t (Tier 2, with an Advanced Conduit Upgrade).

Touching conduits share one energy pool: each segment holds 10,000 NE (Tier 1) or 200,000 (Tier 2), added together, so a long run keeps a reserve. Generators on its sides fill the pool; machines draw from it, highest priority first and equal priorities evenly. Batteries are the backup: they give only what the generators leave short of what the machines want, and they take whatever is left over.

Place it between a generator and a machine and it works: its sides take and give by themselves. The Conduit Wrench changes a side as for the other types. Energy ignores colour channels.

guide.nexium.start.welcome:
Welcome
Nexium adds drawers and barrels, a storage network, conduits, all-in-one tools, Nexium gear and the Essentials.

Pick a topic on the left, or search for one. Most topics end with the recipes for their items.
guide.nexium.start.codex:
Using the Codex
Pick a topic on the left. Click a category to open or close it.

Coloured, underlined words are links: click one to jump there. The < and > buttons go back and forward, and Home comes back here.

Type in the search box to find any topic.

In any inventory, hover over an item and press H to open its page. In a recipe, click an ingredient to open its page.
guide.nexium.start.new:
What's new
1.27.0
One Conduit now carries items, fluids and energy together, with a new look: three strands and a plate that shows each side's direction and colours. An Advanced Conduit Upgrade makes it Tier 2, and old conduit items turn into the new one when you carry them.

1.26.10
New Nexium Nugget (nine make an ingot). Redstone Fuel Rods now take a nugget in the middle instead of an ingot. Fixed the Power Meter saying "Not enough power!" when there was plenty.

1.26.9
The Power Meter has tabs: Generation, Batteries and Using power. A Power Meter used as a conduit facade works as a meter: right-click it with an empty hand for the dashboard (sneak + right-click opens the conduit side menu).

1.26.8
Fixed: right-clicking a conduit with an empty hand now opens its side settings.

1.26.7
Right-click a conduit with an empty hand to open its side settings, like the wrench does. Fixed the Nexium Sword texture and the gap under the conduit energy cap.

1.26.6
The Combustion Generator makes 40 NE/t (twice as much). Every farm, the Iron Farm, the Experience Farm, the Freezer and the Nexus Furnace has an On/Off button on its screen: off, it does no work and uses no power, and it stays off when you pick it up.

1.26.5
The Charging Station shares 4,000 NE/t among the cells charging (one cell gets all of it, four get 1,000 each). Storage and fluid parts need copper, gold and diamond nuggets instead of ingots and diamonds. The Jetpack is back to 8 NE/t thrusting and 4 hovering.

1.26.4
The Redstone Reactor has a 16 bucket water tank: with three slots of blue ice and water, nine rods at +2 settle at 59.9% heat and keep the full 2,700 NE/t. Packed ice now lasts a minute and blue ice two minutes.

1.26.3
The Power Meter now also lists machines that a Battery on the network feeds directly (like a Charging Station touching a Battery), marked fed by a Battery.

1.26.2
The Jetpack uses half the power (4 NE/t thrusting, 2 hovering) and has two keys to set in Controls: Engine On/Off and Hover On/Off. With hover off, hold jump to rise and let go to drop.

1.26.1
The Jetpack is drawn as a pack of its own on your back (two tanks, a battery light and glowing nozzles), not as elytra wings.

1.26.0
The Jetpack: worn in the wings slot, it flies on a battery cell (Iron, Gold or Diamond Cell, charged in the new Charging Station); jump in the air, jump rises, let go to hover, sneak to sink. The Crafting Storage Tablet now runs on a battery cell too. Restocking no longer hands out torches while the Auto Torch module is on.

1.25.20
A Diamond Nugget (nine make a diamond), and diamond tools, weapons, armor and the Diamond AIOT can be smelted down to nuggets in a furnace, blast furnace or Nexus Furnace: a whole one gives what its diamonds are worth and wear takes its share off.

1.25.19
An Edit button beside the filter slot of a conduit side, the Import/Export Bus, the Connectors and the Disk Drive opens that filter to edit it without taking it out. The Disk Drive has a Move to drawers button that pushes its disks' items and fluids into the drawers of a Drawer Controller on its network, only what a drawer already holds or is locked to.

Clicking the result of the Crafting Terminal (and of the Backpack's crafting grid) quickly now crafts on every click: fast clicks used to be read as a double-click and craft nothing.

1.25.18
The Backpack's crafting grid can be hidden with the x in its panel (a small Craft button brings it back, and the Backpack remembers). The Farm Assembler makes the Stone, Copper, Iron, Golden and Diamond AIOTs from raw materials, 11 of the material and 9 sticks, with no tools to craft first, and it is now crafted from just four crafting tables.

1.25.17
Quest rewards are still random items from the mod, but never Compressed blocks or drawers any more.

1.25.16
The AIOT readout and 3x3 outline no longer disappear in the middle of a long mining job: they stay up while you hold the mine button, and fade after the usual time once you stop.

1.25.15
3x3 mining is built into every AIOT now: no module needed. It starts off; switch it on with X or the new 3x3 button in the tool menu, and the tunnel length works as before. The 3x3 Mining Module is retired: one already in an AIOT keeps that AIOT's setting and comes back as its materials when you open the tool menu, and its recipe is gone. A vein, 3x3 or tunnel swing now drops everything where you broke the first block (the aiotDropsAtFirstBlock setting turns that off).

1.25.14
The Combustion Generator's screen no longer says it is making 20 NE/t when its buffer is full: it says it is full and burning, with its power wasted.

1.25.13
The Farm Assembler's From network button now uses the network's water and lava: a line of water or lava buckets takes real buckets first, then makes up the rest from fluid in the network (a Fluid Drawer, a Fluid Tank or a fluid disk), a bucket's worth each. It holds that as fluid and gives it back to the network if you pick another target.

1.25.12
The Trash Can: craft it from a Cauldron and a Hopper. Hoppers, droppers, Item Conduits and Import/Export Buses empty into it and it never fills up; right-click it for a slot that destroys whatever you drop on it. Items only, and nothing it destroys comes back. The Farm Assembler links to a storage network: touch it with a Storage Connector, an Inventory Cable or another network block, and its From network button takes what the chosen target still needs out of the network.

1.25.11
The inventory key (E) closes every Nexium window, as Escape does (not while you are typing in a text box). JEI and REI keep their item lists clear of the Backpack's crafting panel. Nexium tooltips wrap to one narrow width, and a few that said things twice don't. The Power Meter shows what a generator really makes, even when it hands energy straight to a Battery or machine touching it.

1.25.10
The Enchanted Grindstone: craft it from a Grindstone, a Book and Lapis Lazuli. Open it, put an enchanted item or book in the top slot and plain Books in the Book slot, and click an enchantment to pull it onto a book of its own. It is free, curses come off too, and the item keeps its wear and its other enchantments.

The Hostile Mob Switch: make it at the Farm Assembler from 140 hostile mobs of any kind. Right-click it and press Stop hostile spawning: no hostile mob spawns near any player in the whole world until you press it again. Mobs already there stay, spawners and spawn eggs still work, and a redstone signal on a switch follows too.

1.25.9
The Backpack has a Crafting module: a 3x3 crafting grid in its screen, with the recipe book and JEI/REI '+', that refills from the Backpack so shift-click crafts all there is. The Backpack screen also has a trash slot that keeps the last item until you put another in.

1.25.8
The Feeding module has settings: in the Backpack's screen, Eats at N is how hungry you must be before it eats (19 is as soon as any hunger is missing; click lowers it, shift-click raises it), and May waste lets it eat food that restores more than is missing. The default is as before.

1.25.7
Left clicks work in the Advanced Filter's tag picker and in the conduit's Out colour grid, and Enter adds a block in the vein blacklist screen. Nexium smithing recipes no longer need the netherite upgrade template: leave that slot empty.

1.25.6
The Advanced Filter has a Tags button (search and pick any item tag) and a Match button (Smeltable or Furnace fuel); Blacklist flips it. A Smeltable filter on a furnace's top and a Fuel filter on its side fill it from one chest. Conduit arms also show an arrow: out to the block when inserting, in to the conduit when extracting, a double arrow for both.

1.25.5
A conduit side can extract on several colours at once: in its settings, the Out row is a grid of the 16 colours, and a click switches one on or off. What it takes out goes to the insert sides of any of them.

1.25.4
Nothing in the quest book is locked now: every chapter is open from the start and a quest counts as soon as you have done it. Quests you have already met finish at once with their rewards.

1.25.3
Using a villager's trade no longer makes it cost more: prices ignore demand now, and a trade that had gone up is back at its base price.

1.25.2
The free camera has night vision: caves, nights and unlit rooms are as bright as day while it is away from you.

1.25.1
The Drawer quest takes a drawer of any wood or size (a Poplar Drawer did not count before). Every Nexium recipe is in your recipe book when you join a world. The free camera no longer leaves caves and terrain undrawn inside rock or under the world.

1.25.0
The Conduit Scanner: right-click any conduit with it to see everything on that conduit network, what each side connects to, its channel colours, and whether it takes out, puts in or both. Click a connection to outline it in the world, and a red ! marks a dead end. Craft it from a spyglass, a comparator, 2 iron ingots and redstone.

1.24.4
Storage connectors no longer connect to machines (furnaces, hoppers, farms and so on): feed those with an Import/Export Bus. A new setting lists what they refuse.

1.24.3
Fixes: energy conduits no longer leak memory, storage networks no longer load chunks, Builder Undo respects protected areas, and a settings file with a mistake is kept instead of replaced.

1.24.2
Zoom: hold the Zoom key (pick one in Key Binds) and scroll to zoom in more or less. The free camera has no fog now.

1.24.1
Reinforced Glass: tinted glass that the Wither, the Ender Dragon and explosions can't break. Craft 8 from 8 glass around an obsidian block.
Vein mining works with any tool or an empty hand now, on Left Control, and a new setting lists blocks it never takes.
Zoe bites 1.5 times as hard, and the eye that was painted on the back of her head is gone.

1.24.0
Zoe the dog: a follower that behaves like a tamed wolf, cannot be killed, and scares creepers away. Craft her Dog Egg from 5 bones and 4 leather. She can wear Wolf Armor or the new Nexium Dog Armor.

1.23.1
Two key names on the Key Binds screen were too long and ran under their buttons; they are shorter now.

1.23.0
One mod id, nexium, instead of two. Worlds saved with older versions do not load: their blocks and items have new ids. The settings file is now config/nexium.json (the old one is ignored). Quests give a random item from the mod.

1.22.6
The Power Meter: put it against an Energy Conduit for a dashboard of the whole network, with priority and an off switch for each machine. A quest book with six chapters that gives random Nexium items. A settings screen: every setting of the config file, grouped by feature, with Reset buttons, from the Settings button in the Codex or the armor menu (or Mod Menu, or a key you choose). Storage networks also scan far faster when many buses or terminals share one.

1.22.5
The full Nexium set gives Water Breathing too, so you can't drown. It has its own switch in the armor menu.

1.22.4
Placing with the Diagonal Placement key: aim at the middle of a face and the block goes straight across from it with a one block gap (aim near an edge for the diagonal one). The face you aim at is drawn in zones, a middle square and a trapezoid toward each edge, and the zone used is filled in gold.

1.22.3
The Backpack has a Restocking Module: stacks you use up in the hotbar and offhand are topped up from the Backpack at 8, and it unpacks Compressed and storage blocks when it has to. Every stackable item stacks to 1,024 in the Backpack, so the Torch Stack Module is retired. The Fluid Intake pulls 8 buckets a second and holds 32.

1.22.2
The Lock Upgrade is a Drawer Key now: right-click a drawer with it to lock it and again to unlock it. It is never used up and fits any drawer; there is no lock slot any more. Old Lock Upgrades are keys, and a drawer that held one stays locked and drops the key.

1.22.1
Item conduits pull the output of the one-block farms, the Iron Farm and the Freezer from any side (hoppers still from below). The Freezer has the OC overclock button too. Packed ice now takes 22.5 seconds and blue ice 45.

1.22.0
Overclock: every one-block farm, the Iron Farm and the Experience Farm has an OC button at the top right of its screen. It steps the farm through off, x2, x4 and x8 (Shift-click goes back): it works that many times faster for that many times the NE/t, so a cycle costs the same energy at any speed. Short of energy it runs as fast as it can pay for.

1.21.25
The Nexus Link no longer takes shulker boxes or ender chests: they drop where they were, even in a vein or a 3x3.

1.21.24
The Disk Drive screen has a Move up button beside Move to disks: it moves what the lower tier disks in that drive hold onto its higher tier disks (items to item disks, fluids to fluid disks), as far as there is room.

1.21.23
Free camera: the speed now changes with Left Ctrl and the scroll wheel (the plain scroll wheel does nothing), and the experience bar and level number are hidden while it is on.

1.21.22
Free camera: press K to fly the camera through everything while your player stays put. Villagers' trades never run out, and C in the trading screen gives a villager nobody has traded with a new set of trades. Mending now repairs any damaged item in your inventory, not only what you hold. Nine sponges craft a Large Sponge (reach 14), nine of those a Huge Sponge (reach 32) and nine of those a Giant Sponge (reach 64); they soak up that much water, turn wet, and dry in a furnace.

1.21.21
13 more blocks have Compressed, Double Compressed and Triple Compressed versions holding 9, 81 and 729: calcite, dripstone block, smooth basalt, terracotta, sandstone, red sandstone, obsidian, magma block, mud, clay, soul sand, soul soil and snow block. Snow blocks, clay, amethyst blocks, glowstone, honeycomb blocks, magma blocks, melons, dripstone blocks and resin bricks now craft back into what made them, so the Backpack's Compacting Module packs the snowballs, clay balls, shards, dust, honeycomb, magma cream, melon slices, pointed dripstone and resin bricks too.

1.21.20
The Backpack's Compacting, Feeding and Auto Torch modules now keep working while its screen is open: blocks are packed, food is eaten and torches are taken from the slots you are looking at, instead of waiting until you close it.

1.21.19
The Backpack can be sorted: press O (Sort Inventory in Controls) with the mouse over its slots and they sort A to Z like a chest, with torches merged to 512 while the Torch Stack module is on and the modules left alone. Sorting your inventory while a Backpack is open no longer moves the Backpack you opened it from.

1.21.18
Hold Left Alt (change it under Controls > Key Binds) and right-click with a block to place it diagonally, off the edge of the face you aim at. An outline shows where it will go: white when the cell is free, red when it is taken.

1.21.17
Compressed blocks: stone, cobblestone, deepslate, cobbled deepslate, tuff, granite, diorite, andesite, netherrack, blackstone, basalt, end stone, dirt, sand, red sand and gravel each have a Compressed, Double Compressed and Triple Compressed block holding 9, 81 and 729 of them. The Backpack's Compacting Module packs them by itself. What you collect from the Experience Farm and the Nexus Furnace now repairs your Mending items first, as an orb does. A shulker box shows a grid of what is in it under its name. The Backpack's slots are evenly spaced.

1.21.16
Two more Backpack modules: Feeding eats food from the Backpack when your hunger bar is missing at least what the food restores, so none is wasted (never foods with side effects), and Compacting packs what the Backpack holds into storage blocks, such as 9 iron ingots into an iron block. The Torch Stack Module now stacks torches to 512.

1.21.15
The Backpack: a backpack slot above the magnet slot for a Backpack (8 leather around a chest) that holds 36 stacks and has 5 module slots. Press B to open the worn one, or right-click one in your hand. The Auto Torch Module places torches from it within 32 blocks, spaced so nothing hostile can spawn, even behind walls and in unseen caves. The Torch Stack Module makes torches stack to 256.

The 3x3 tunnel steps are off, 2, 3, 8, 16, 24 and 32: hold Z and scroll to change it without opening the menu. Shift-clicking the Crafting Terminal's result crafts at most 2 stacks a click.

1.21.14
Captured Mobs show more: their variant or colour always (a frog's, a sheep's, a villager's job), and with Shift held their age, owner, gear and status.

1.21.13
The Experience Farm: made at the Farm Assembler from 64 Bottles o' Enchanting, it makes 40 XP a second on 10 NE/t, banks up to 200 levels' worth, and you collect it with Collect all, +1 level or +10 levels.

1.21.12
The Import/Export Bus screen has six buttons to choose the side it faces (only sides with an inventory or tank). The Crafting Terminal starts A to Z. The scroll wheel no longer pulls items out of bundles. The Nexus Furnace gives ten times the experience, and the Collect XP number now matches what you receive.

1.21.11
The scroll wheel over a stack moves one item to or from the other inventory (down sends, up pulls). The Nexus Furnace is back to 30 NE/t a slot, and a Redstone Fuel Rod lasts 96 hours. Tier 1 item and fluid conduits make 8. The Infinite Lava Source takes an eye of ender, the Elevator chiseled deepslate, and the Nexium ingot no longer needs an upgrade template.

1.21.10
Fixed: a Battery on an Energy Conduit now charges from Solar Panels and other generators, and gives back only what the machines are short of. Energy Conduits move 2,500 NE/t (Tier 1) and 50,000 NE/t (Tier 2) and hold 10,000 / 200,000 NE a segment; the Tier 1 recipe makes 8. The Solar Panel makes 30 NE/t (8 in rain) and stores 5,000 NE. The Nexus Furnace uses 10 NE/t a slot. Shift + click and drag also moves items between the hotbar and the inventory.

1.21.9
The Nexus Furnace: eight smelting slots at once on Nexus Energy, smelting, blasting and smoking in one.

1.21.8
Space + left click moves every stack of an item to the other inventory; shift + click is vanilla's single stack again, and shift + click and drag still moves everything you cross.

1.21.7
The stonecutter turns a block of quartz back into 4 quartz.

1.21.6
Shift + click moves every stack of that item, and shift + click and drag moves everything the cursor crosses. Sorting is now the O key (separate from JEI's R), works with the mouse over an item, and is just A to Z. The unused Honey fluid is removed.

1.21.5
Three creative tabs: Nexium Storage, Nexium Tools, and Nexium Farms & Power.

1.21.4
Recipe tweaks: stairs make 8, trapdoors 12, slabs and stairs craft back into blocks, universal dyeing, craftable coral blocks and blackstone, and more. Shulkers drop 2 shells and budding amethyst drops with Silk Touch.

1.21.3
The Tree Farm can grow Poplar. The Redstone Reactor makes twice the power (200 NE/t a rod at the default depth) and stores 1,000,000 NE. The Froglight Farm makes 5 of each froglight a cycle.

1.21.2
Energy Conduits share one pool that holds energy (2,000 NE a Tier 1 segment, 16,000 a Tier 2), and Batteries no longer starve farms: machines are served first.

1.21.1
Farms need only power: no bread, gold, feed or bone meal, and no boosts. The Livestock Farm now makes every animal's drops.

1.21.0
The Tree Farm makes the logs of the tree you pick, or chorus fruit.

Power: every farm and the Freezer run on Nexus Energy. Make it with the Combustion Generator, Solar Panel, Thermal Generator or the Redstone Reactor, store it in Batteries and carry it with Energy Conduits. Every farm's filler is now 576.

1.20.3
Fixes: the Construction Builder places fresh blocks (no doubled slabs, no grown crops), Exchange gives what the old blocks drop, a broken builder drops its module, farms no longer lose output when nearly full, and shift-click crafting in the terminal keeps what your inventory has no room for.

The Monster Farm's Totem of Undying is now a 2% find. The Warden and the Elder Guardian cost 10 levels to pick up.

Comparators read drawers (how full they are) and farms (how full the output is, and 15 when stopped).

1.20.2
The Froglight Farm makes ochre, verdant and pearlescent froglights from frogs, slimes and glass.

1.20.1
The Bee Farm makes honey bottles in its output slots. The Gourd and Cactus Farm makes all four at once. The Iron Farm no longer makes poppies. The Moss Farm makes resin too. Cleaner Nexium Spear textures. The sort key's message shows on top.

1.20.0
Press R over a container or your inventory to sort it (never the hotbar). Press again for the next order: A to Z, creative menu, biggest stacks.

1.19.0
Ten more one-block farms at the Farm Assembler: Monster, Nether Mob, Ocean, Slime, Livestock, Crop, Gourd and Cactus, Generator, Bee (with honey) and Moss. The Assembler's list scrolls.

1.18.1
The Crafting Terminal's search and its recipe book's search are linked: type in either.

1.18.0
Four more one-block farms at the Farm Assembler: Witch, Sugar Cane, Bamboo and Nether Wart. The Villager Breeder now takes 10 minutes, not 20.

1.17.1
Right-click a terminal's or the Codex's search box to clear it.

1.17.0
Vein mining (V) now takes stone too, and grasses, bushes and leaf litter, a whole patch at once.

1.16.1
The AIOT's 3x3 and vein outline shows for 20 seconds after you switch to it or press X, Z or V, like the readout.

1.16.0
Digital storage: the Disk Drive holds 8 storage disks, 16k to 4M items or 64 to 16,384 buckets each. Move to disks empties chests onto them.

1.15.0
The Construction Builder builds out from the block you click, with modes, a size, Undo and a Nexus Link.

Right-click a grown crop to harvest and replant it; hold V for the whole field.

The Nexium Ingot is made from a diamond, an emerald, a netherite ingot and a netherite upgrade template.

1.14.5
Drawers are cheaper: planks and slabs, no chest.

1.14.4
The anvil is never Too Expensive: any job can be done for its full cost in levels.

1.14.3
The terminal search follows JEI's and REI's, and their + button shows exactly which ingredients are missing.

1.14.2
Connector priority always comes first: items go to the highest priority inventory that takes them.

The Drawer Controller's reach outline now needs sneak + right-click; a plain right-click shows the drawer count.

1.14.1
The AIOT readout by the hotbar shows for 20 seconds when you switch to an AIOT or press X, Z or V.

1.14.0
The Farm Assembler makes the one-block farms and the Master Librarian: pick one, put in what it needs, press Build. No more renaming chests.

1.13.1
The AIOTs are redrawn at 32x32 in their original colours, and the Fortune and Silk Touch colours show on the gem.

1.13.0
The guide is now the Nexium Codex: one long page per topic, links, search, and H to look up any item.

Every texture is redrawn at 64x64, with new AIOTs and new Nexium armor.

The Dimensional Anchor always loads its 3x3 chunks, and right-clicking it shows them for a minute.

1.12
Five more one-block farms, the Freezer, soul sand to sand in a blast furnace, and Vein Mining without a module.
guide.nexium.start.finding:
Finding things
Every item's tooltip says what it does. Every item is in one of three Nexium creative tabs: Storage, Tools, and Farms & Power.

Press L for advancements: the Nexium tab is a map of the whole mod.

Lost your guide? Craft a book with any drawer.
guide.nexium.start.keys:
Key binds
G: tool menu, when holding an AIOT or Nexium tool. With neither: the armor menu.
Left Control: hold to vein mine, with any tool or an empty hand.
M: Magnet on or off.
B: open the Backpack worn in the backpack slot.
O: sort the chest, Backpack or inventory under the mouse.
Left Alt: hold while right-clicking with a block to place it diagonally.
C: in a villager's trading screen, new trades for a villager nobody has traded with.
K: free camera on or off.

Zoom, Open Nexium Settings and Open Quests: no key until you pick one. Hold Zoom and scroll the wheel to zoom in more or less.

Change them in Options > Controls > Key Binds, under Nexium.
guide.nexium.start.settings:
Settings
Every setting can be changed on the Nexium Settings screen: the Settings button at the top of this Codex or in the armor menu, Mod Menu's Configure button, or the Open Nexium Settings key (unbound until you pick one). Each has a Reset, and hovering one says what it does.

They are saved in the config file, nexium.json, and apply at once in a world you host. On a server, the server's file counts.

Install Nexium on the server and on every player's game.
guide.nexium.drawers.drawers:
Drawers
A drawer stores one kind of item in huge amounts.

1x1: 54 stacks.
1x2: 2 slots of 27.
2x2: 4 slots of 13.5.

All 13 woods, made from that wood's planks and slabs (no chest). Capacity upgrades multiply these.
guide.nexium.drawers.using:
Using a drawer
Right-click the front: insert what you hold.
Double-click: insert all matching items from your inventory.
Left-click the front: take a stack.
Sneak + left-click: take one.

Break a drawer by hitting any side but the front.
guide.nexium.drawers.bar:
Fullness bar
A bar under each count shows how full it is, upgrades counted:
green: under 75%
yellow: to 90%
red: 90% and up

No bar when empty, unless locked. Fluid and compacting drawers have one too.

A comparator reads the same fullness: 0 when empty, 15 when full. A drawer with 2 or 4 sections reads their average.
guide.nexium.drawers.upgrades:
Upgrades
Right-click a drawer with an upgrade to install it.
To see or remove them: right-click a side or the top empty-handed (or sneak + right-click).

Four slots take capacity and Void upgrades; a fifth takes only Lock.
guide.nexium.drawers.capacity:
Capacity upgrades
Iron x2
Gold x4
Diamond x8
Emerald x16
Netherite x32

They add together: Iron + Gold = x6. No upgrades = x1.
Not removable if the contents would no longer fit.
guide.nexium.drawers.swap:
Swapping upgrades
All four slots full? A better capacity upgrade swaps out the weakest.

Right-click the drawer with it: the old one drops.

Or put it in a slot (shift-click, or click it on): the old one goes to your inventory.
guide.nexium.drawers.lockvoid:
Lock and Void
Drawer Key: right-click a drawer with it to lock it, and again to unlock it. A locked drawer keeps each slot reserved for its item, even when empty; padlock top-right on the front. The key is never used up and fits any drawer, compacting drawer or fluid drawer.

Void Upgrade: deletes what doesn't fit (handy for cobble farms). Marker top-left. Overflow is destroyed for good!
guide.nexium.drawers.fluid:
Fluid Drawer
Holds 32 buckets of one fluid.

Use a bucket on the front to fill or empty it.

Capacity, Lock and Void upgrades work too. A Fluid Intake next to it fills it.
guide.nexium.drawers.compacting:
Compacting Drawer
Stores nuggets, ingots and blocks as one pool (any 9-to-1 or 4-to-1 recipe that works both ways).

54 stacks of the largest form, e.g. iron blocks.

Top slot: largest form. Bottom: smaller forms.
guide.nexium.drawers.moving:
Moving storage
Breaking a drawer, compacting drawer or fluid drawer keeps everything inside, upgrades included, in the dropped item, like a shulker box.

Hover over the item to see what is inside. Place it anywhere to get it all back.
guide.nexium.drawers.controller:
Drawer Controller
Drawers touching it, or each other, within 12 blocks join it.

Right-click with an item: it goes to the drawer holding it.
Double-click: your whole inventory.
Empty hand: shows its drawer count.
Sneak + empty hand: shows its reach for 1 minute (again to hide).
guide.nexium.drawers.slave:
Controller Slave
Extends a controller. Place it touching the drawers, or the controller, within 12 blocks of the controller; drawers within 12 blocks of the slave join too.

Slaves chain: a slave within reach of another slave works as well.
guide.nexium.drawers.barrels:
Barrels
Five tiers of barrel:
Iron: 45 slots
Gold: 66 slots
Diamond: 84 slots
Emerald: 102 slots
Netherite: 120 slots

Iron has 5 rows of 9, the rest 6 rows of 11, 14, 17 and 20. Bigger ones get a wider screen.
guide.nexium.drawers.barrelup:
Barrel upgrades
Right-click a barrel with a Barrel Upgrade to raise its tier in place. What is inside stays inside.

Iron: a vanilla barrel
Gold: an Iron Barrel
Diamond: a Gold Barrel
Emerald: a Diamond Barrel
Netherite: an Emerald Barrel
guide.nexium.network.network:
Storage network
A storage network joins many inventories into one big storage, opened from a Crafting Terminal.

No power needed. One network holds up to 2048 cables, connectors and terminals.
guide.nexium.network.connector:
Storage Connector
Joins every storage inventory touching it to the network: chests, barrels, drawers, shulker boxes.

It does not join machines: furnaces, blast furnaces, smokers, brewing stands, hoppers, dispensers, droppers, crafters and the machines of Nexium itself. Feed those with an Import/Export Bus on the face you want. Which blocks a connector refuses is a setting you can change.

Right-click it to set its priority. Items go into the higher priority first, even if a lower one already holds some, and come out of the lower first. At the same priority, items join their own kind.

A Drawer Controller only fills drawers that already hold the item or are locked to it.
guide.nexium.network.filtered:
Filtered Connector
Joins only the one storage inventory it faces, through a filter. Like the Storage Connector it does not join machines (use an Import/Export Bus for those).

Right-click it to set its priority and put a filter in its slot. It accepts only what the filter lets through.

Craft it from a Storage Connector and a comparator.
guide.nexium.network.cable:
Inventory Cable
Joins network blocks into one network. It links Storage and Filtered Connectors, Crafting Terminals, other cables, Fluid Intakes and Dimensional Outputs.

Cables and connectors grow an arm towards each block they link to.
guide.nexium.network.terminal:
Crafting Terminal
Shows everything in the network, fluids first, beside a crafting grid.

Left-click: take a stack.
Right-click: take one.
Shift-click: to your inventory. On the crafting result it crafts up to 2 stacks per click.
Holding items: left-click puts all in, right-click puts one in.
guide.nexium.network.search:
Search and sort
Type to search by name. Start with @ to search by mod: @minecraft shows only vanilla items.

An arrow button flips the direction; another cycles the sort: # count, A name, @ mod. It starts on A to Z.

Hover an item for its count.
guide.nexium.network.extras:
Terminal extras
Bucket on a fluid fills it. A full bucket: left-click pours it in, right-click stores it.

Red X: empties the grid into the network, else your inventory, else the floor.

Bars by the result slot show how full the network is.
guide.nexium.network.crafting:
Crafting from it
The recipe book shows what you can make from the network's items. Click a recipe to fill the grid from the network, then your inventory.

JEI and REI: their + button does the same. When something is missing, JEI marks those slots red and REI lists them. Their search box and the terminal's stay the same. Neither mod is needed.
guide.nexium.network.bus:
Import/Export Bus
Place it on an inventory or tank, next to a cable.

Import: pulls items and fluids in.
Export: pushes them out.

Right-click: mode, the side it faces (six buttons, only sides with an inventory or tank) and an optional filter. 32 items or a bucket every half second.
guide.nexium.network.emitter:
Level Emitter
Connect it to the network. It gives a redstone signal while the network holds at least (or fewer than) an amount of one item.

Right-click it: click the slot with an item, set the amount, choose at least or fewer than. A bucket counts that fluid, in buckets.
guide.nexium.network.tablets:
Tablets
Sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with a Crafting Storage Tablet to link it.

Right-click the tablet anywhere, in any dimension, to open that network while the terminal's chunk is loaded (an Anchor can keep it so).

The tablet runs on a battery cell: sneak and right-click it to put one in. Opening costs 100 NE (1,000 from another dimension), and the open screen 2 NE a tick.
guide.nexium.network.anchor:
Dimensional Anchor
Keeps the 3x3 chunks around it loaded, all the time: the chunk it stands in and the 8 around it.

When you place it, and whenever you right-click it, it outlines those chunks for 1 minute: the chunk borders as a grid at its height, with posts at the four outer corners. Right-click again to hide the outline.

Removing it lets the chunks unload. Chunks forced by /forceload or other mods stay loaded.
guide.nexium.disks.drive:
Disk Drive
Holds 8 storage disks on a storage network: place it against a cable, connector or terminal.

Right-click it for its screen, or right-click it holding a disk to put the disk in. Its lights: green has room, yellow is over 75% full, red is full.
guide.nexium.disks.disks:
Storage disks
An item disk holds a number of items, of any kinds: 16k (16,000), 64k, 256k, 1M or Nexium (4,000,000).

Fluid disks hold 64, 256, 1,024, 4,096 or 16,384 buckets. A disk keeps what it holds when moved, dropped or put in another drive.
guide.nexium.disks.priority:
Priority and filter
Drives start at priority 10, above chests at 0, so new items go to disks first. Shift-click the buttons to step by 10.

A Basic or Advanced Filter in its slot limits what goes onto its disks.
guide.nexium.disks.move:
Move to disks
The button in a drive's screen moves what the network's chests and barrels hold onto the disks, as far as they have room.

Drawers keep their items.

Move up, beside it, moves what the lower tier disks in that drive hold onto its higher tier disks (items to item disks, fluids to fluid disks), the biggest first, as far as there is room. Disks of the same tier are left alone.
guide.nexium.disks.crafting:
Making disks
A Disk Casing and a Storage Part make a disk. A 16k part: redstone, copper nuggets and lapis (a bucket for a fluid part).

Three parts and a gold nugget, a diamond nugget, an emerald or a Nexium ingot make the next size. Sneak + right-click an empty disk to take it apart.
guide.nexium.links.links:
Dimensional links
Send items and fluids anywhere: any distance, any dimension.

Click a Dimensional Input with a Dimensional Link Card, then click any Outputs.

What you put in the Input arrives at the Outputs.
guide.nexium.links.names:
Link names
Each link has a random name. To choose one, rename the card in an anvil first, or rename it later in either block's screen.

Look at an Input or Output to see its name for 3 seconds.
guide.nexium.links.moving:
Moving an Input
Break it, then click the new one with the same card. It takes over the link and all its Outputs.
guide.nexium.links.input:
Dimensional Input
Takes items and fluids: by hand, or from hoppers, pipes, conduits and Fluid Intakes.

If nothing can take an item, its buffer backs up.
guide.nexium.links.dspeed:
Transfer Speed
The Transfer Speed Upgrade goes in a Dimensional Input's speed slot.

One: 16 items at a time.
Two: full stacks.
guide.nexium.links.output:
Dimensional Output
Pushes what arrives into everything around it, on the sides you turn on: inventories, fluid storage, storage network blocks and item conduits (which carry items on to their Insert sides of the same colour).

Inputs are skipped.
guide.nexium.links.sides:
Output sides
In an Output's screen, the D, U, N, S, W and E buttons switch sides on and off (green is on). Hover one to see what is on that side.

An Output can hold a filter, so one Input can split items by type.
guide.nexium.links.conduits:
Conduits
One Conduit carries items, fluids and Nexus Energy together, 16 colour channels of each. Every side has its own mode, colour, filter and redstone setting for each of the three.

Tier 1:
Items: 4 every half second.
Fluids: 100 mB a tick.
Energy: 2,500 NE a tick.

An Advanced Conduit Upgrade, used on a conduit, makes it Tier 2: items 16 every half second, fluids 2000 mB a tick, energy 50,000 NE a tick.
guide.nexium.links.scanner:
Conduit Scanner
Right-click any conduit to open a window with its whole network, one conduit type at a time (a tab each: Item, Fluid, Energy).

Every side that ends at a block is listed with the block, where it is, its mode, priority, filter and redstone setting. It changes nothing: the Conduit Wrench does that.

A red ! marks a problem. Hover a row for what it is.
guide.nexium.links.scanner2:
Reading the window
Grouped (the default): one heading per channel colour, with what takes things OUT of a block and what puts them IN under it. List: one row per side, with its In colour and its Out colours.

Warnings: nothing inserts on an extractor's channel, nothing extracts on an inserter's, redstone is holding the side off right now, or it is paused.

Click a row to outline that conduit and block in the world for ten seconds; click it again, or Clear outlines, to remove it. Energy has no channels: its conduits share one pool.
guide.nexium.links.wrench:
Conduit Wrench
Right-click a conduit side: cycle its mode (off, insert, extract, both).

Sneak + right-click: all its settings.

Right-click a conduit with a full block to give it a facade. The wrench takes it off.
guide.nexium.links.channels:
Colour channels
Each side has an In (insert) and an Out (extract) colour.

What a side extracts goes to sides inserting on the same colour. A Both side can use different colours in and out.

Arm rings: inner = In, outer = Out.
Arm arrow: out to the block = In, in to the conduit = Out, both ways = Both.
guide.nexium.links.settings:
Side settings
Sneak + wrench opens a side's settings: mode, the In colour, the Out colours (click any of the 16 to switch it on or off: a side can extract on several), redstone control, priority, round-robin, filter and speed upgrades. It names what is on that side.

Conduit Speed Upgrade: faster. Up to 3 fit in the speed slot.
guide.nexium.links.filters:
Filters
Basic Filter: right-click to set up to 9 items to allow or block.
Advanced Filter: also matches whole item tags, e.g. every ore. Its Tags button picks any tag by name, and its Match button adds Smeltable or Furnace fuel.
Blacklist flips all of it.
Fluids: use their bucket.

Filters go in a conduit side, Output, Filtered Connector or Bus.

Furnace: Smeltable on its top and Fuel on its side fill it from one chest.
guide.nexium.links.intake:
Fluid Intake
Takes fluid from the source blocks touching it, up to 8 buckets a second (it holds 32), and passes it to a Fluid Drawer, conduit or network next to it. Infinite water is never drained.

Bucket on it: take only that fluid. Sneak + empty hand: any again.
guide.nexium.links.lava:
Lava Source
The Infinite Lava Source: put it next to a Fluid Intake for endless lava. It never runs dry.

Craft it from obsidian, lava buckets and an eye of ender.
guide.nexium.links.limits:
Reach and limits
Dimensional links: any distance, any dimension.

Fluid Intake: the blocks touching it.

One conduit line: up to 1024 conduits.
guide.nexium.aiot.aiot:
All-in-one tools
A pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe and sword in one item, in Stone, Copper, Iron, Golden, Diamond, Netherite and Nexium.

It mines what its material's tools mine, as fast as the best of them. An iron AIOT can't mine obsidian; a diamond one can.
guide.nexium.aiot.crafting:
Crafting one
Put all five tools of one material (pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, sword) anywhere in the crafting grid.

Five fresh tools make a full AIOT, worn ones a worn one. The anvil repair cost of the most expensive tool carries over.
guide.nexium.aiot.stats:
Stats
Durability, 1.5 times that of the five tools:
Stone 983
Copper 1,425
Iron 1,875
Golden 240
Diamond 11,708
Netherite 15,233
Nexium 18,750

Attack damage: 9, 9, 9, 7, 9, 10 and 11.
guide.nexium.aiot.fighting:
Fighting
Hits as hard as that material's axe, at a sword's speed (1.6 attacks a second). It sweeps like a sword and disables shields like an axe.

It loses 1 durability per hit and per block mined.
guide.nexium.aiot.using:
Using an AIOT
Right-click: strips logs, scrapes or unwaxes copper, makes paths (or tills a path into farmland), puts out a lit campfire.

Sneak + right-click: tills grass and dirt.

Every tool and sword enchantment works.
guide.nexium.aiot.enchants:
Enchantments
Crafting keeps every enchantment, at the highest level any tool had it.

Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods: the highest stays (Sharpness wins a tie).

Curses stay too.
guide.nexium.aiot.silk:
Silk and Fortune
Both stay: Fortune is active, Silk Touch inactive (the tooltip says so). Switch in the tool menu.

At an anvil, an AIOT with one takes the other from a book or AIOT, added inactive. A grindstone removes the inactive one too.
guide.nexium.aiot.upgrade:
Netherite AIOT
At a smithing table: a Diamond AIOT and a netherite block. Leave the template slot empty.

Enchantments (the inactive one too) and wear stay.
guide.nexium.aiot.upgrade2:
Nexium AIOT
At a smithing table: a Netherite AIOT and a Block of Nexium. Leave the template slot empty.

Or craft one from five Nexium tools.
guide.nexium.aiot.menu:
Tool menu
Hold an AIOT or Nexium tool and press G; press it again or Esc to close.

Mining: switches Silk Touch and Fortune. The gem shows which: green Fortune, blue Silk Touch.

Haste II: Nexium tools only.
guide.nexium.aiot.menu2:
Tool menu, more
3x3 mining: switches it on or off. Modules (AIOTs only): one slot, for the Nexus Link.

Vein size: click to step 4, 9, 18, 32 ... up to the server's limit, then back to 4.

Armor: opens the armor menu.
guide.nexium.aiot.modules:
AIOT modules
One module slot: the Nexus Link, whose drops go to a storage network. It keeps its on/off setting when taken out.

3x3 mining and vein mining need no module: both are built into every AIOT.
guide.nexium.aiot.nexuslink:
Nexus Link
Sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with the module (or an AIOT that has one) to link it.

Drops, Fortune and Silk Touch included, go into that terminal's network in any dimension. Experience still drops.
guide.nexium.aiot.nexuslink2:
Nexus Link, more
The terminal's chunk must be loaded: put a Dimensional Anchor near it.

What the network can't take drops as usual.

Shulker boxes and ender chests are never taken: they drop where they were.
guide.nexium.aiot.area:
3x3 Mining
Mines the 3x3 around the block, facing you: a wall ahead, the floor or ceiling looking down or up.

Only blocks the AIOT is made for, about twice as hard as yours at most, never ones with contents.

Built into every AIOT, off until you switch it on: X, or the 3x3 button in the tool menu.
guide.nexium.aiot.tunnel:
Tunnels
Tunnel sets how deep a 3x3 digs, away from you: off, 2, 3, 8, 16, 24 or 32 layers. Click it in the tool menu, or hold Z and scroll the wheel: up for deeper, down for shallower. It stops at off and at the deepest, and the hotbar does not change while Z is held.

A faint green outline shows what your next block will take, for 20 seconds after you pick the AIOT or press X, Z or V. Sneak mines one block.
guide.nexium.aiot.vein:
Vein Mining
Mines every touching block of your kind: ores, stone, logs, leaves, obsidian. Grasses, bushes and leaf litter go together.

Hold Left Control while mining, with any tool or an empty hand (the block must be one the tool is right for). No module needed: an AIOT's tool menu sets how many blocks, any other tool takes up to the limit (256). Blocks on the blacklist in settings are never vein mined.
guide.nexium.builder.builder:
Construction Builder
Right-click a block to build out from it: every connected block of that kind gets a new one on the face you clicked.

It places the block in your offhand, or else the one you clicked, facing the same way. A pale blue outline shows where they will go.

Each one is a freshly placed block: a crop is planted, not grown. A double slab uses two slabs.
guide.nexium.builder.modes:
Modes and tiers
Extend: the whole connected face. Line: one row, the way you look. Exchange: swaps the face for your offhand block and gives you what the old ones drop when broken (cobblestone for stone).

One click places up to 9 (Iron), 27 (Diamond), 64 (Netherite) or 128 (Nexium, unbreakable). Each block costs 1 durability.
guide.nexium.builder.menu:
Builder menu
Press G holding the builder for its menu: mode, plane (any, flat or upright) and size.

Undo takes back your last build and returns its blocks. It remembers 2 builds, until you log out.
guide.nexium.builder.link:
Blocks from a network
Put a Nexus Link Module in the builder's menu, then sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with the builder to link it.

When your inventory runs out of a block, it takes more from that network. Creative players need no blocks.
guide.nexium.builder.crafting:
Crafting one
Iron: paper, lapis and a gold nugget over an iron frame.

Add a diamond to make it Diamond. Its settings and module stay.
guide.nexium.builder.upgrade:
Upgrading
At a smithing table, template slot empty: Diamond + netherite ingot makes Netherite, and Netherite + Nexium ingot makes Nexium.
guide.nexium.aiot.readout:
Outline and readout
Blocks the next swing would also take glow pale green.

A panel by the hotbar shows Silk Touch or Fortune and each module's state for 20 seconds after you switch to an AIOT or press X, Z or the vein key, and while it is held.

Change the time or turn it off in client settings.
guide.nexium.aiot.both:
Mining rules
With 3x3 also on, holding the vein key vein mines; without it, the 3x3 mines.

Fortune, Silk Touch and Nexus Link apply; each block costs 1 durability.

Sneak: one block only.
A broken AIOT drops its modules.
guide.nexium.nexium.nexium:
Nexium
The tier above netherite: tools, armor and a block, all from Nexium ingots. Everything Nexium survives fire and lava.

Nexium armor and its set bonuses are in this category too; the Nexium AIOT is under All-in-one Tools.
guide.nexium.diamond_nugget.nugget:
Diamond Nugget
Nine nuggets make a diamond, and a diamond makes nine nuggets.

Smelt a diamond tool, weapon, armor piece or Diamond AIOT in a furnace, blast furnace or Nexus Furnace to get nuggets back: a whole one gives what its diamonds are worth (a pickaxe 27, a sword 18, boots 36, leggings 63), and wear takes its share off, so a half worn pickaxe gives about 14, never fewer than one. A stack holds 64, so the chestplate and the AIOT give 64.
guide.nexium.nexium.ingot:
Nexium Ingot
A diamond, an emerald and a netherite ingot, in a crafting table, make 3 ingots.

Nine Nexium Nuggets make an ingot, and an ingot makes nine nuggets. A nugget is the centre of a Redstone Fuel Rod.
guide.nexium.nexium.block:
Block of Nexium
Nine ingots make a block, and a block makes nine ingots again.

It is a beacon base, mined like a netherite block. Beacons take the ingots as payment.

At a smithing table it turns a Netherite AIOT into a Nexium AIOT.
guide.nexium.nexium.gear:
Nexium gear
At a smithing table: the netherite piece and a Nexium ingot, template slot empty. Enchantments and wear stay.

There is a Nexium sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, spear, helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.
guide.nexium.nexium.tools:
Nexium tools
Netherite's mining speed and level, 2,500 uses (netherite 2,031) and enchantability 18.

One more attack damage than netherite: sword 9, axe 11, spear 6.
guide.nexium.nexium.spear:
Nexium Spear
Charges and attacks like a vanilla spear, one step past netherite on each spear stat.

It is a netherite spear plus a Nexium ingot at a smithing table.
guide.nexium.nexium.haste:
Haste II
The Nexium pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe and AIOT give the real Haste II effect while held in the main hand.

With Efficiency V they mine as fast as netherite with Efficiency V under a Haste II beacon: stone and netherrack break instantly.
guide.nexium.nexium.haste2:
More on Haste II
Like the beacon's, it also speeds up attacks by 20%.

It shows a steady infinity icon and goes when the tool is put away.
guide.nexium.nexium.haste3:
Haste, beacons
It doesn't stack with a beacon's Haste II. A beacon's or command's Haste is never taken off.

Switch it off in the tool menu (G).
guide.nexium.armor.armor:
Nexium armor
Helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.

Armor: 4 / 9 / 7 / 4 points, 24 in all (netherite 20).
Toughness: 5 each, 20 in all: the game's maximum.
Knockback resistance: 0.15 each.
Durability: 484 / 704 / 660 / 572.
guide.nexium.armor.extras:
Also
It takes armor trims, shown on the item icons too. Baby zombies and the like wear it properly.

Like netherite, it keeps piglins calm. It survives fire and lava.
guide.nexium.armor.bonuses:
Set bonuses
Nether-forged (full set): Fire Resistance.

Miner's set (full set): full-speed mining underwater and in the air.

No knockback (full set): hits and explosions don't push you back.
guide.nexium.armor.bonuses2:
More bonuses
Nexus restock (full set, linked chestplate): hotbar stacks top up from a storage network, and you eat from it when hungry.

Water breathing (full set): Water Breathing, so you can't drown.

Night vision (helmet): Night Vision.
guide.nexium.armor.menu:
Armor menu
Press G with no AIOT or Nexium tool in hand, or click Armor in the tool menu. Each bonus has an on/off switch; bonuses the worn pieces don't give are greyed out.

A setting is saved on the piece that carries it, so it moves with the armor.
guide.nexium.armor.effects:
Effects
Fire Resistance, Water Breathing and Night Vision are infinite while worn, with a steady icon. They go as soon as a piece comes off or the bonus is switched off.

A potion's or beacon's effect is never taken away.
guide.nexium.armor.restock:
Nexus restock
Link the chestplate: sneak + right-click a Crafting Terminal with it.

A hotbar stack you use is topped up from the network at 8 left, or refilled when you use the last one. A stack you move or throw away whole is left alone.
guide.nexium.armor.restock2:
Eating from it
When your hunger bar is down by 6 or more, you eat the most filling plain food in the network, never food with effects (golden apples, rotten flesh, pufferfish). Bowls and bottles go back in.

The network is reached as for the Nexus Link module.
guide.nexium.essentials.explosions:
Explosions
Creeper and ghast explosions break no blocks, and ghast fireballs light no fires. They still hurt and push players and mobs.

They also spare item frames, paintings, armor stands, dropped items, minecarts and boats.
guide.nexium.essentials.harvest:
Right-click harvest
Right-click a fully grown crop to harvest it: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa. It is replanted from its own seeds.

Hold the vein mining key (Left Control) to harvest the whole connected field at once. Sneak to use an item on the crop instead.
guide.nexium.essentials.tnt:
Endermen and TNT
TNT, beds, respawn anchors, withers and end crystals work as in vanilla.

Endermen never pick up blocks. One that was already carrying a block before the mod was added can still put it down.
guide.nexium.essentials.slots:
Extra slots
Five slots that use no inventory space.

Above the offhand slot: the backpack slot (the Backpack), the trinket slot (the Magnet) and the wings slot (an elytra, or any modded item that glides like one).

Under the crafting grid: the arrow slot and the totem slot.
guide.nexium.essentials.slots2:
Using the slots
Shift-click a Backpack, Magnet, elytra, arrows or totem to send it to its slot, or right-click a Magnet or elytra in your hand to put it on (sneak + right-click for a Backpack).

In the creative inventory they sit right of the armor.
guide.nexium.essentials.slots3:
Slots and death
The slots are saved with you. On death they drop like the rest of your inventory (Curse of Vanishing destroys), unless keepInventory is on.
guide.nexium.essentials.arrows:
Arrow slot
Holds up to 64 arrows of any kind.

Bows and crossbows shoot from it after anything held in a hand and before arrows in your inventory.

Picked-up arrows fill it first.
guide.nexium.essentials.totem:
Totem slot
Takes a Totem of Undying, or any item with death protection.

If you would die with no totem in either hand, this one saves you, with the same effects as a held one. A held totem is used first.
guide.nexium.essentials.wings:
Wings slot
An elytra here glides exactly like one in the chest slot, so you can wear a chestplate too.

It wears down the same way; Unbreaking and Mending work, and its protection enchantments add to your armor's (80% cap still applies). Other players see it.
guide.nexium.essentials.magnet:
Magnet
Works while it is in your trinket slot. It pulls every item and experience orb in range, even through walls, using the normal pickup: full inventories, pickup delays and item owners still apply.
guide.nexium.essentials.magnet2:
Using the Magnet
Sneak + right-click: range 4, 8, 12 or 16 blocks.

M: on or off. It glints while on.

It pulls back what you drop after the 2-second pickup delay, so switch it off before throwing things away.
guide.nexium.essentials.backpack:
Backpack
Worn in the backpack slot, above the trinket slot, it holds 36 stacks, as much as your whole inventory, and has five module slots. It uses no inventory space.

Sneak + right-click it to wear it. Press B to open the worn one, or right-click one in your hand.
guide.nexium.essentials.backpack2:
Using the Backpack
Put items in and take them out like any chest. Shift-click moves a stack between it and your inventory. A Backpack can't hold another Backpack.

Every stackable item stacks to 1,024 in its slots, whatever it stacks to elsewhere.

Press O with the mouse over its slots to sort them A to Z, as in a chest. Stacks merge to 1,024, and the modules stay where they are.

What is in it stays with the item: it drops with everything in it when you die (unless keepInventory is on), and can sit in a chest.
guide.nexium.essentials.backpack_modules:
Backpack modules
Modules go in the five slots at the right of the Backpack's screen; each kind fits once. The button beside a module switches it on or off. They work while the Backpack is worn, even with its screen open.

So far: Auto Torch, Feeding, Compacting, Restocking and Crafting.

The old Torch Stack module is retired: every stackable item stacks to 1,024 in the Backpack now, so it does nothing and no longer fits a slot.
guide.nexium.essentials.auto_torch:
Auto Torch
Places torches from the Backpack wherever a hostile mob could still spawn within 32 blocks of you, in every direction: in the open, in caves behind walls, even in caves nobody has seen. It reads the real light, so it never lights what is already lit.

It does nothing in the Nether (torches can't stop spawns there), in adventure or spectator mode.
guide.nexium.essentials.auto_torch2:
Where the torches go
As far apart as they can be and still leave no dark block: a torch lights 13 blocks each way, so on open ground they end up in a staggered grid about 19 blocks apart.

Each sweep places up to 8. It stops when the Backpack has no torches left, and carries on when you put more in.
guide.nexium.essentials.restocking:
Restocking
While the Backpack is worn, a stack you are using up in the hotbar or the offhand (blocks you place, arrows you shoot) is topped up to a full stack from the Backpack when it gets down to 8, or refilled when the last one is used.

Only use counts: a stack you move or throw away whole is left alone. It does nothing in creative mode.
guide.nexium.essentials.restocking2:
Unpacking
If the Backpack has none of the item left but holds a bigger form of it, Restocking unpacks just enough: Triple Compressed stone becomes Double Compressed, then Compressed, then stone, and what you did not need stays in the Backpack. An iron block unpacks into ingots, and a block of anything that crafts back into the same items does.

Renamed, enchanted and other customised items are never unpacked.
guide.nexium.essentials.feeding:
Feeding
While the Backpack is worn, it eats for you. Once a second it checks how much of your hunger bar is missing, and eats the food in the Backpack that restores the most without any of it being wasted.

It never eats foods with side effects, such as rotten flesh, pufferfish, golden apples or chorus fruit. It does nothing in creative mode.
guide.nexium.essentials.feeding2:
Feeding settings
In the Backpack's screen, under the module slots:

Eats at: it waits until your hunger bar is at or below this level, 19 of 20 at first (as soon as any hunger is missing). A click lowers it, shift-click raises it.

No waste: it eats only food that fits the missing hunger. May waste: at its level it eats the best fit even if some is lost, or the smallest food.
guide.nexium.essentials.crafting_module:
Crafting Module
With it installed (and switched on), the Backpack's screen has a 3x3 crafting grid and a result slot in a panel at its right.

Put items in the grid by hand, or open the recipe book (the book button under the grid) and click a recipe, or use the + button of JEI or REI: the grid fills from what the Backpack holds first, then your inventory. After every craft the emptied grid slots refill from the Backpack, so shift-click on the result crafts all you have.
guide.nexium.essentials.crafting_module2:
Crafting Module
Made with iron ingots in the corners, planks (any kind) on the four sides and a crafting table in the middle.

The x in the corner of the panel hides the grid (what is in it goes back into the Backpack) and the small Craft button in its place shows it again; the Backpack remembers which. Take the module out or switch it off and what is in the grid goes back into the Backpack, as it does when you close the screen.
guide.nexium.essentials.backpack_trash:
Trash
The Backpack's screen has a trash slot under the module column. It is always there: no module is needed.

Drop an item on it to get rid of it. The item stays in the slot, so you can take it back, until you put another in or close the screen.
guide.nexium.essentials.enchanted_grinds:
Enchanted Grindstone
A grindstone that takes enchantments off one at a time and puts each on a book of its own, instead of wiping them all. It costs no experience.

Right-click it. Put an enchanted item or book in the top slot and plain Books in the Book slot, then click an enchantment in the list. It comes off onto a new Enchanted Book, using up one Book. The item keeps its wear, its name and everything else on it.

Enchanted Grindstone
Made from a Grindstone, a Book and Lapis Lazuli, anywhere in the crafting grid.

Curses come off too. A book that holds just one enchantment has nothing to separate. An AIOT's waiting Silk Touch or Fortune is listed and taken off like the rest. A long list scrolls with the mouse wheel, and closing the screen gives back what is in the slots.

The plain Grindstone still wipes enchantments for experience, as before.
guide.nexium.essentials.trash_can:
Trash Can
A bin that destroys items. Craft it from a Cauldron and a Hopper, anywhere in the crafting grid.

Pipe items into it: a hopper, a dropper, an Item Conduit or an Import/Export Bus pointing at it from any side empties into it, and it never fills up. Right-click it for a screen with one slot: drop an item on the slot and the whole stack is destroyed (a right click destroys one).

Only items are destroyed: it takes no fluids or energy. Whatever goes in is gone for good, so point nothing at it that you want to keep.
guide.nexium.essentials.trash_can2:
Trash Can
It keeps nothing, so it is also a way to stop a machine from backing up: a farm piped into a Trash Can never fills its output.

A Shift-click in its screen moves nothing, so an item is only ever destroyed by dropping it on the slot on purpose. Storage Connectors do not connect to it, so it never takes what is on a storage network.

The Backpack has a trash slot of its own, which keeps the last item until you put another in.
guide.nexium.mobs.hostile_switch:
Hostile Mob Switch
A block that turns hostile mob spawning off for the whole world. Right-click it and press Stop hostile spawning; press again to let them spawn.

While it is on, no hostile mob spawns near any player, in any dimension, and a switch anywhere in the world is the one setting: every switch shows the same state. Mobs already there stay. Spawners and spawn eggs still work.
guide.nexium.mobs.hostile_switch2:
Hostile Mob Switch
Made at the Farm Assembler from 140 hostile mobs of any kind (zombies, creepers, endermen and so on), as spawn eggs or Captured Mobs.

It covers what Peaceful does to spawning: the usual spawn cycle, phantoms, patrols, and the spawns of portals, reinforcements, endermites and creakings. A redstone signal on a switch stops spawning; losing it lets spawning start again.

Breaking the switch leaves the setting as it was, so keep one to turn it back.
guide.nexium.essentials.compacting_modul:
Compacting Module
While the Backpack is worn, it packs what the Backpack holds into storage blocks once a second: 9 iron ingots into an iron block, 9 nuggets into an ingot, 9 wheat into a hay bale. The blocks go in the Backpack's own free slots; with no room, nothing is packed.

It only uses packs that craft straight back, the same ones the Compacting Drawer uses, so nothing is lost: sand never becomes sandstone. Renamed or enchanted items are left alone.
guide.nexium.essentials.compressed:
Compressed blocks
Twenty-nine bulk blocks have compressed versions that hold 9, 81 and 729 of them in one block.

Stone: stone, cobblestone, deepslate, cobbled deepslate, tuff, granite, diorite, andesite, calcite, dripstone block, smooth basalt, terracotta, sandstone, red sandstone, obsidian.

Nether and End: netherrack, blackstone, basalt, magma block, end stone.

Soil and snow: dirt, mud, clay, sand, red sand, gravel, soul sand, soul soil, snow block.
guide.nexium.essentials.compressed_craft:
Crafting them
Nine of a block craft into its Compressed block, nine of those into a Double Compressed block, and nine of those into a Triple Compressed block. Each crafts back into nine of the one below, with nothing lost.

Ice is not on the list: nine ice already make packed ice, and nine packed ice make blue ice.
guide.nexium.essentials.compressed2:
Using them
A compressed block is mined like the block it stands for, with the same tool and at the same speed, and drops itself. Its tooltip says how many it stands for.

A Backpack's Compacting Module packs them by itself: 729 cobblestone in the Backpack become one Triple Compressed Cobblestone. A Compacting Drawer holds a block and its compressed versions as its tiers.
guide.nexium.essentials.way_back:
Way back
Some packs in the game had no way back, so the Compacting Module skipped them. Now each of these blocks crafts back into exactly what made it, and the Backpack packs them too:

Snow block: 4 snowballs. Clay: 4 clay balls. Amethyst block: 4 shards. Glowstone: 4 dust. Honeycomb block: 4 honeycomb. Magma block: 4 magma cream. Melon: 9 slices. Dripstone block: 4 pointed dripstone. Resin bricks: 4 resin bricks.

Loose dust, honeycomb, cream and shards are packed 4 at a time until you unpack them.
guide.nexium.essentials.sponges:
Combined sponges
Nine sponges craft a Large Sponge, nine of those a Huge Sponge, and nine of those a Giant Sponge. Each crafts back into nine of the one below.

A sponge soaks up water next to it and turns wet. These reach further and take more: the Large Sponge reaches 14 blocks and takes 585 water, the Huge Sponge 32 blocks and 5,265, the Giant Sponge 64 blocks and 47,385.
guide.nexium.essentials.sponges2:
Drying them
A wet sponge dries in a furnace (a Large one in 10 seconds, a Huge one in 20, a Giant one in 40), or at once in the Nether, and is ready to soak again.

The Backpack's Compacting Module packs sponges by itself: nine in the Backpack become a Large Sponge. A Giant Sponge soaking a big sea can make the game stutter for a moment.
guide.nexium.essentials.free_camera:
Free camera
Press K to take the camera off your player. You stay where you are while the movement keys and the mouse fly the camera through everything: forward goes where it looks, jump goes up, sneak goes down, sprint is faster, and Left Ctrl with the scroll wheel changes the speed (the plain scroll wheel does nothing).

Nothing you click reaches the world while it is away, and the experience bar is hidden. There is no fog and it has night vision while the camera is away, so you see clearly to the edge of the loaded world, even underwater, underground or at night. Zoom works from the camera too. Press K again to come back. It ends by itself if you are hurt. Change the key under Controls > Key Binds, in Nexium.
guide.nexium.essentials.villagers:
Villagers
Their trades never run out: every trade can be made as often as you like and none is ever locked. Using a trade never makes it cost more either: prices ignore demand.

Trade cycling: in the trading screen press C to give a villager nobody has traded with a new set of trades, as often as you like. Once you have traded with a villager, or it has any experience, its trades stay. Change the key under Controls > Key Binds, in Nexium.
guide.nexium.essentials.mending:
Mending anywhere
Experience orbs repair any damaged item with Mending in your inventory, not only what you hold or wear: the hotbar, the main inventory and the extra slots too.

Each orb picks one at random, at the usual rate of 2 durability a point. The experience from the Experience Farm and the Nexus Furnace does the same.
guide.nexium.essentials.diagonal:
Diagonal placement
Hold Left Alt (change it under Controls > Key Binds, in Nexium) and right-click a block with a block in your hand to place it diagonally: one out from the face you click and one over toward the nearest edge of that face. Aim near the top of a wall and the block lands diagonally up and out; near its left edge, diagonally left. On the block you aim at, the face is drawn in zones, a middle square and a trapezoid toward each edge, and the one you are aiming at is filled in gold.

Aim at the middle square instead and the block goes straight across from it with a one block gap: two out, nothing between.

The block touches the one you clicked only along an edge and may float, so staircases, roofs, diagonal lines and pillars need no support first. It uses up the item as usual, never replaces a block, and follows the same build rules as any placement.
guide.nexium.essentials.elytra:
Elytra enchanting
At an anvil, elytra take Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection and Projectile Protection from enchanted books, and can hold all four at once, like any other armor piece now.
guide.nexium.essentials.enchants:
Higher levels
Protection (all four kinds), Unbreaking, Looting, Fortune and Respiration go up to level V: in the enchanting table, at an anvil (two IVs make a V), in loot chests and from villagers.

The anvil is never Too Expensive: any job can be done for its full cost in levels.
guide.nexium.essentials.enchants2:
Fewer limits
Mending works with Infinity, every protection goes on one piece, and Sharpness works with Smite.

Bane of Arthropods still excludes both, and Fortune still excludes Silk Touch.
guide.nexium.essentials.piglins:
Piglins
Any piece of netherite armor counts as gold armor: piglins stay neutral. Bartering still uses gold ingots.
guide.nexium.essentials.elevator:
Elevator
A flat Nexium platform. Put elevators at different heights in the same column (same X and Z), anywhere from the bottom of the world to the top.

Right-click one for the list of floors and click one to go there.
guide.nexium.essentials.elevator2:
Floors
Name the floor in the box and press Name; an empty name goes back to Floor 1, 2, 3 from the bottom. A floor with no room to stand (the two blocks above it are blocked) is greyed out.

Breaking an elevator forgets its name.
guide.nexium.essentials.librarian:
Master Librarian
At a Farm Assembler: pick Master Librarian, put in 12 villagers (spawn eggs or Captured Mobs) and press Build. He comes out as a Captured Mob: right-click a block to let him out.
guide.nexium.essentials.librarian2:
His trades
A book of every enchantment at its highest level, Mending and the other treasure ones too, but no curses. Prices are the villagers' own: 2 to 64 emeralds, plus a book each.

A librarian made this way can't be used as one of the 12.
guide.nexium.essentials.debris:
Ancient debris
Drops netherite scrap: 2 per block, multiplied by Fortune like diamond ore (Fortune I, II and III average 2.67, 3.5 and 4.4, up to 8). Silk Touch drops the block.
guide.nexium.mobs.mobs:
Picking up mobs
Sneak + right-click a mob with an empty hand to pick it up. You get a Captured Mob item that looks like its spawn egg, with a glint.

Right-click a block with it to let the mob out.
guide.nexium.mobs.kept:
What it keeps
A Captured Mob keeps everything about the mob: health, name, equipment, saddle and chests, villager profession and trades, horse stats, owner and age.

Its tooltip shows its variant or colour (a frog's, a sheep's, a villager's job) and, with Shift held, its age, owner, gear and status.
guide.nexium.mobs.limits:
Mob limits
The Ender Dragon and the Wither can't be picked up. The Warden and the Elder Guardian cost 10 experience levels. Only a pet's owner can pick it up.

Not in Adventure mode, nor inside spawn protection (unless you are an operator).
guide.nexium.mobs.know:
Good to know
Sneak + right-click a tamed horse, donkey or llama with an item still opens its inventory.

A picked-up villager gives up its bed and workstation; it finds new ones when let out.

Riders get off and a lead drops.
guide.nexium.mobs.know2:
The item
Monsters can't be let out on Peaceful (the item stays in your hand).

A Captured Mob item never despawns and survives fire, lava, explosions and cactus.
guide.nexium.mobs.elixir:
Bedrock Breaking
Drink the Elixir for 5 minutes of Bedrock Breaker: a diamond or netherite pickaxe (or AIOT) then mines bedrock like obsidian.

Bedrock drops nothing, and any bedrock breaks, even the bottom layer above the void. Careful!
guide.nexium.mobs.assembler:
Farm Assembler
Makes the one-block farms, the Master Librarian, the Hostile Mob Switch and plain Stone to Diamond AIOTs from raw materials (11 of the material and 9 sticks, what their five tools cost). Right-click it, pick one from the list on the left and put in what it needs.

The right side shows how much of each material is in, with a bar, and a tick when a line is done.
guide.nexium.mobs.assembler2:
Filling it
Add from inventory moves everything it still needs out of your inventory. Shift-clicking items, or hoppers above or beside it, add them too.

It only takes what is still needed, and picking something else gives back what was in. With a Storage Connector or an Inventory Cable against it, From network fills it from that storage network, and water and lava buckets are made up from the network's water and lava, a bucket's worth each. When all is in, press Build and take the result from the slot.
guide.nexium.mobs.farm:
Iron Farm
A one-block iron farm. Place it anywhere.

Every 7.5 seconds it makes a golem's drops: 3-5 iron, about 1,900 iron an hour.
guide.nexium.mobs.farm2:
Using the farm
Right-click it to see the output and a bar to the next golem. It needs only Nexus Energy: 40 NE/t.

Hoppers take the output from below; item conduits can take it from any side. Nothing can be put in. The OC button runs it x2, x4 or x8.
guide.nexium.mobs.make:
Making one
At a Farm Assembler: pick Iron Farm in its list, put in the materials below and press Build. The Iron Farm appears in the slot next to the button.
guide.nexium.mobs.recipe:
Iron Farm recipe
Zombies: 4
Villagers: 12
Torches: 33
Slabs: 20
Signs: 16
Trapdoors: 12
Beds: 12
Smooth Stone: 576
guide.nexium.mobs.notes:
Recipe notes
Zombies and villagers can be spawn eggs or Captured Mobs (zombie, husk, drowned or zombie villager all count).

Torches, slabs, signs, trapdoors and beds can be any kind.
guide.nexium.mobs.notes2:
Recipe notes, more
Amounts are totals: any mix of kinds counts, in any order. The Assembler only takes what is still needed and its screen shows what is missing.
guide.nexium.mobs.running:
Running the farm
When the output is full, there is no power, or a redstone signal reaches it, the farm waits. The screen says which.

A comparator reads how full the output is, and 15 once the farm has stopped for lack of room.

Breaking it drops the Iron Farm with its progress kept.
guide.nexium.mobs.farms:
More farms
Twenty more one-block farms, made at the Farm Assembler like the Iron Farm. Mobs can be spawn eggs or Captured Mobs.

Hoppers below take the output, item conduits from any side; redstone pauses it. The OC button runs a farm x2, x4 or x8.

A comparator reads how full the output is, and 15 once the farm has stopped for lack of room.
guide.nexium.mobs.breeder:
Villager Breeder
2 villagers, 4 beds, 2 composters, 8 hay bales, 2 emerald blocks, 576 planks.

A baby villager (Captured Mob) every 10 minutes.
guide.nexium.mobs.barter:
Piglin Barter Farm
2 piglins, 9 gold blocks, 16 soul sand, 16 planks, 576 netherrack.

The real piglin barter loot every 6 seconds.
guide.nexium.mobs.zpiglin:
Zombified Piglin Farm
